variable reactance transformer models are needed for real-time security analysis functions, and that a variable reactance model is not always needed for state estimation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of real-time security assessment functions for use in the real time control center.
modeling of three-winding transformers and two-winding transformers with a large variation of leakage reactance over the transformer tap range.
the modeling and estimation of variable impedance transformers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
variable impedance models are needed for accurate state estimation of transformers with variable leakage reactances.
a variable leakage reactance transformer model must be used in real-time security analysis functions.
a variable impedance transformer model is necessary in the real-time security analysis function for the proper representation of two-winding and/or three-winding transformers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of variable impedance models for transformers has been a success.
the models are not as simple as the traditional constant reactance models, but the additional complexity is well worth the effort.
the variable leakage reactance transformer model has been implemented in our real-time state estimation and load-flow functions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transformer leakage reactance can be a significant variable and should be included in the model.
the traditional constant reactance models used in real-time security analysis functions are not always adequate.
transformer models must be carefully selected for use in security analysis functions.
